title: Bake the sun rays from two colour-neutral masks held beside the creature sprites
context: The phone's noon cost (18.9 ms against 13.3 ms at midnight, Note10+ on Impeller OpenGL ES) is the sun rays: a 120-segment disc mesh drawn every frame with drawVertices and BlendMode.modulate against a many-stop sweep gradient. The Mac's noon cost is the lake glints instead. Baking the rays into one image gave 13.2 ms. On devices the landscape fills its byte budget exactly (40 MB full screen, 22 MB page).
options: Bake the rays in the painter with a static cache (records vector art in a frame and leaks images)
Bake the rays in MeadowLayers inside the landscape budget (lowers landscape density on devices)
MeadowRays records two colour-neutral masks once at build and tints an image from them when sunColour or raysGlowAlpha changes; held by the stage's _SceneImages beside the creature sprites
outcome: Chosen: MeadowRays in lib/features/garden/render/meadow_rays.dart, with colour-neutral masks recorded once and image-only tinting. It keeps the no-vector-after-build rule and leaves the landscape budget alone. The tinted masks match today's rays within 3 levels on Skia and 5 on Impeller. The owner chose to fold it into PR #245. Built by a follow-up mitosis run (~/.mitosis/field-notes/impeller/rays-run.zsh, --no-push) on mitosis/meadow-impeller.
